heading: Training that spreads safety past the first tokens, and whether it holds up
definition: training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens, and whether it holds up.
summary: Follow-up studies on Llama, Gemma, Qwen and other families, a few sharing authors with the original, find that such training sharply cuts prefilling attack success and partly helps against GCG. Whether the gains hold up is contested: an adaptive, rank-based prefilling attack, later benign fine-tuning and some prompt jailbreaks defeat deepened models.

suggested_status.by_scale: 1-10B: R2 for scoped gains against ordinary prefilling, and partly against GCG, on deepened Llama-2-7B-Chat and Gemma-2-9B-IT. Author overlap is not identifiable from the pack headers, so R1 cannot be ruled out. C for durability: rank-based prefilling and benign SFT defeat deepened Llama-2-7B-Chat and Gemma-2-9B-IT. Paraphrasing attacks on Gemma-2-9B-IT give a scope limit, with AutoDAN the only failure. 10-100B: R2 for scoped improvements of other deepening methods, with attack and model limits. <1B: R0 for the SRP setting (360M). >100B: untested. Toy: no empirical reproduction established; formal theory is separate.
suggested_status.reason: C applies to the durable, general reading ('whether it holds up'), not to the scoped gains. Scoped gains: non-original tests report deeper positional KL (arXiv:2503.03710#K03). On the original's data-augmented Llama-2-7B-Chat checkpoint, ordinary prefilling gives a harmfulness score of 0.001, versus 0.831 for the undeepened chat model (arXiv:2512.05518#r2; these are scores, not percentages). Durability failures: on that same checkpoint, intermediate-human rank-based prefilling (RAP) recovers a harmfulness score of 0.6731 (arXiv:2512.05518#r4). Deep Alignment Gemma-2-9B-IT refusal at prefill depth 100 falls from 90% to 10% after 50 benign Alpaca SFT steps (arXiv:2510.18081#R9). The same Gemma model under paraphrasing attacks is a scope limit, not a failure. Base→Deep Alignment ASR is AutoDAN 92%→94%, PAIR 70%→60% and TAP 88%→78% (verdict text, no row); only AutoDAN fits challenges. counts: versions.V7.studies_by_size shows coverage at <1B, 1-10B and 10-100B, none above 100B. versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.training and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.attack show both training and robustness tests. The original baseline is arXiv:2406.05946#r52. counts: versions.V7.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 3, but the pack headers do not say which studies share authors.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would a deepened model survive rank-based prefilling and unrestricted benign or harmful fine-tuning? Such a result would move the durability reading from C toward R2. Do RAP and benign-SFT erosion also defeat the original recipe on other families and in matched settings? Would ordinary-prefilling protection fail on a matched re-run? That would challenge the scoped gains too. Identifying which studies share authors with the original would settle R1 versus R2. Measuring positional safety, adaptive-attack robustness, fine-tuning durability and capability cost together on the same models would mark the boundaries of the fix.

source.title: Safety alignment should be made more than just a few tokens deep
source.authors: Xiangyu Qi; Ashwinee Panda; Kaifeng Lyu; Xiao Ma; Subhrajit Roy; Ahmad Beirami; Prateek Mittal; Peter Henderson

original_result.setup: They fine-tuned Llama-2-7B-Chat on 256 safety recovery examples that return to a refusal after up to 100 prefilled harmful tokens, plus benign utility examples.
original_result.result: On HEx-PHI, prefilling attack success fell from 42-57% to 2.8-4.5% for 5 to 40 prefilled tokens, and GCG success fell from 36.5% to 18.4% (HEx-PHI) and from 65.6% to 19.0% (AdvBench). Later benign fine-tuning kept attack success at or below 3.8%, but harmful-example, identity-shifting and backdoor fine-tuning still reached 53.9-80.0%.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Backtracking training cut prefill attack success and kept sampled outputs nearly as safe as greedy.
DPO on synthetic course-correction data made Llama2-Chat 7B recover from harmful prefills more often.
Decoupled refusal training cut LLaMA3-70B success on several jailbreaks to 0–6.5% and added late refusals.
A2D cut prefilling and DIJA attack success on diffusion LMs to 0–3.8%.
AlphaAlign RL sharply cut jailbreak success on two 3B models, mostly beating refusal SFT.
Extended-refusal models kept most refusals after abliteration, while standard models lost most.
Deep-alignment training cut Llama-2-7B average attack success from 47% to 12% on AdvBench.
BSAFE backtracking training cut prefill jailbreaks to 5–9% and survived small harmful fine-tunes.
Harmful-prefix augmentation and DeepRefusal cut Llama3-8B prefilling success from 82.7% to near zero.
DeepAlign held GCG and adaptive prefill attack success to 0–2.2% on Llama-2, Mistral and Qwen.
The authors report FalseReject tuning kept KL divergence high past the first five tokens.
HumorReject training kept safety at 95–100% under five prefix attacks on two models.
Dual-objective DOOR and prefix-augmented training shifted outputs at later tokens too, nearly ending prefilling attacks.
Data augmentation nearly eliminated prefilling, while PRESTO cut AutoRAP harmfulness to 0.05–0.16.
Deep SFT sharply cut plain harmful-question attack success on three Qwen audio models.
Targeted completion cut Llama-2-7B prefill success to 0.5% and GCG success to 0.4%.
SafePath R-8B stayed safe under a compliant reasoning prefill; its safety-primer phrase reappeared later in reasoning.
DeepAlign Llama2-7b-chat stayed at 0% harmfulness after 10-shot malicious fine-tuning.
Llama2-7B with an explicit safety signal held prefill attack success at or below 2.7%.
Reproduced Deep Token training kept Llama-2-7B-Chat's safety score at 95.38, versus 3.27 for SFT.
RA training cut LLaDA priming-attack success from 15–89% to 0–8.3%.
MOSA cut LLaDA-8B attack success to 2–9%, including under adaptive middle-targeting attacks.
Safe-role fine-tuning had lower attack success under prefilling than a matched SFT baseline across tested models.
Safety reflections (SRP) in pretraining and SFT cut unsafe compliance under prefilling from 64.24 to 7.47.
Prefill-position consistency training drove held-out prefill attack success to 0.0% on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-3-27B.
Augmented RT cut average jailbreak success to 3.3–3.6 on Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B and Gemma2-2B.
TSC-GRPO and constrained SFT kept LLaMA-2-7B-Chat attack success at 1.6–4.6% after harmful fine-tuning.
HARC cut PAIR, PAP and DeepInception success to near zero on Llama and Qwen.
Dual-objective DOOR training raised refusal of narrative-wrapped attacks to 87.1–97.8% on Qwen3-4B and GLM-4-9B.
Trajectory alignment cut injection success to 0–5% and Qwen2.5-7B prefilling success to 0–4.6%.
Step-wise reflection training reached about 89–100% defense success under AutoDAN, GCG and PAIR.
Prefix-conditioned refusal training cut Llama-3-8B prefilling success to 0.6% at all prefix lengths.
With their decision step forced to COMPLY, aligned defender models stayed far safer than unaligned ones.
Augmenting training with counter-aligned (unsafe) prefills raised safety scores under adversarial prefill to 97.4–99.4.
Prefill deepening cut matched prefill attack success on Llama-2 from 75–84% to 2.7–13.2%.
A recovery-penalty objective provably bounds recovery probability from below at every position.
Output-level consistency training (BCT) cut acceptance of prefill-attack prompts to zero.
Backtracking left 16.5–60% attack success under GCG, AutoDAN and adaptive attacks.
Course-correction gains were small on Qwen2 7B, and GCG and CipherChat success stayed 25–50%.
Constrained SFT left Llama3-8B harmfulness high under harmful LoRA fine-tuning.
DeRTa left 21.5–24.0% attack success under CodeAttack and PAIR and raised over-refusal.
A2D left 11–23% attack success under PAIR and ReNeLLM prompt attacks.
Token-wise constrained fine-tuning failed to offset harmful rates on some models, notably Mistral 7B.
On Qwen2.5-7B, shallow refusal SFT matched AlphaAlign on PAIR and JailbreakTrigger.
Extended refusal gave small Llama-2 gains and left Qwen failing 41–44% on WildJailbreak.
Deep-alignment Gemma-2-9b-it refused only 47–61% of prefills at depth 500.
Qi et al.'s constrained fine-tuning failed under prefill, reaching 80.3% attack success on HEx-PHI.
Prefix augmentation alone left 76.6–77.7% attack success under refusal-direction attacks and 50% under GCG.
DeepAlign still let out-of-distribution harmful prefixes succeed 7.6–9.8% of the time.
FalseReject tuning left prefilling attack success at 27.5–48.5% despite its deeper per-token KL shift.
As baselines, DeRTa stayed vulnerable to Template+Prefill, and DeepAug and DeRTa raised benign over-refusal.
Deepened models gave only partial gains on transferred suffix attacks and barely improved on Crescendo.
PRESTO reduced RAP harmfulness to 0.05–0.16 but did not eliminate it.
Deep SFT raised benign over-rejection on all three Qwen audio models.
Targeted completion left Qwen-2.5-7B at 44.3% prefill success and eroded under benign fine-tuning.
Prefilling raised SafePath R-7B's harmfulness score from 12.7 to 18.6.
DeepAlign's fine-tuning protection eroded with 50–100 harmful shots and nearly vanished on the base model.
Explicit safety signals left 2–10% DeepInception success and proved sensitive to hyperparameters.
Extended-refusal examples cut abliteration (weight-orthogonalization) attack success from 0.98 to 0.36, not to zero.
Deep Token degraded Llama-3.2-1B safety and math accuracy; the study's DSS stayed partly vulnerable to prefilling.
Deep alignment cut attack success only to 59.42 under the LogitsTrap attack, which suppresses refusal tokens.
Refusal-aware denoising alignment cut DIJA success on LLaDA-8B but did not eliminate it.
RA left substantial attack success under very late injection, DiJA, GCG and ReNeLLM.
MOSA left 8–15% attack success under complex-narrative attacks such as Avatar and Speakeasy.
Prefilling still raised safe-role fine-tuning's attack success on base models, to 23.28 on Gemma.
Safety-reflection (SRP) deepening did not survive open fine-tuning: adversarial fine-tuning raised attack success to 79.50.
Augmented RT left Gemma2-9B's average attack success at 38.1 and sharply raised over-refusal.
Triggered backdoors partly eroded TSC-GRPO safety, and some jailbreaks kept 17–25% success.
HARC left substantial CodeAttack success, and about 160 harmful fine-tuning examples undid its gains.
Deep alignment raised refusal of narrative-wrapped attacks only partly; dual-objective DOOR barely helped the 1.7B model.
Abrupt-refusal LoRA tuning helped mainly on one incomplete-prompt pattern and often hurt on unseen patterns.
Trajectory alignment's gains depended on the judge, with 8–16% residual Qwen attack success.
A2D lowered MaskForge-Embed attack success on Dream-Instruct only from 94.0% to 85.0%.
Deep alignment narrowed Gemma-2-9B's attack-success gap under non-imperative rephrasing only from 25% to 19%.
Soft-SFT realignment held only in the matched channel, rebounding to 36.4 under the raw template.
Shallow-Align deepening gave small direct-attack gains on LLaMA-3.1-8B and weak indirect-attack defense.
SafeThinker left 11.5–13.6% prefilling success on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct.
Constrained SFT cut fine-tuned Llama-2-7B-Chat attack success from 15.4 to 3.3, short of the original 0.0.
DeepAlign left Llama3.1-8B's harmfulness score at 20.7–30.1 under mixed harmful fine-tuning.
Defender training's safety gain under harmful prefills decayed as prefills lengthened and was marginal on Qwen3.
DeepAug only partly raised prefill defense rates on LLaMA3-8B and Mistral-7B.
Prefill-augmented training on reasoning models gave reward-dependent results and lowered safety on standard prompts.
Prefill-deepened models stayed vulnerable to insertion attacks and prefills beyond the training span.
Theory predicts that the deeper safety extends into a response, the more capability it costs.
Backtracking SFT alone rarely reset under optimization attacks; attack success stayed near or above baseline.
Course-correction training cut PAIR and AutoDAN attack success by only 1–2 points.
Harmful-prefix augmentation alone did not lower CodeAttack or PAIR success.
Deep Alignment Gemma-2-9b lost most prefill refusal after 50 benign fine-tuning steps.
The token-wise constrained loss did not stop a two-stage benign fine-tuning attack on Llama2-7b.
DeepAug kept Llama3 safety at only 3–59% under prefill-based and AutoDAN attacks.
The RAP attack largely survived data-augmentation deepening of Llama 2.
Deep Token scored below vanilla SFT on AdvBench under a response-adaptation attack.
Safe-role fine-tuning raised Qwen2.5-3B attack success under prefilling above both SFT and the original model.
Trajectory alignment raised Mistral-7B prefilling attack success on AdvBench under the OM judge.
DeepAug barely helped against Template+Prefill and cut LLaMA3's AutoDAN defense rate.

untested.what: Deepening-training effectiveness and durability above 100B parameters.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V7.studies_by_size and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size contain no >100B category. Reported large-model tests remain within 10-100B.

untested.what: Empirical implementation and validation of the theoretical recovery-penalty objective: its recovery-probability guarantee (stated for positions beyond the harm horizon) and its predicted capability cost.
untested.basis: arXiv:2603.04851 reports theoretical derivations and no trained-model evaluation of the recovery objective, the robustness guarantee or the capability cost. Its Limitations leave open whether finite-capacity models can implement the objective and whether finite training reaches it. The training coverage in counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.training concerns other interventions.

untested.what: A joint longitudinal test on the same deepened models: harmful-completion positional KL before and after unrestricted later fine-tuning, together with adaptive inference attacks.
untested.basis: The original optimizes GCG suffixes separately against each victim model, including the augmented model (Appendix A.4: 50 harmful behaviors, 500 optimization steps, three most successful of ten runs). Its Conclusion still lists future adaptive attacks as a limitation, and it reports no joint evaluation of post-fine-tuning positional KL and inference attacks. DOOR lacks later-fine-tuning tests; targeted completion lacks trained-model positional KL; SRP lacks positional measurement. counts: versions.V7.main_rows_by_operation and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation give operation totals but do not establish this joint design.

wording_issues.phrase: training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens
wording_issues.issue: The version groups distinct interventions: later-position recovery augmentation, early-token update constraints, activation-space defenses, classification-assisted decoding, and diffusion-step alignment. Success of an early-token constraint does not itself demonstrate later-token safety.

Measures differ in what they establish. FalseReject's per-token KL (figure only; Gemma-2-2B in R12) is measured on 1,000 FalseReject instruction-response pairs whose responses are classified as refusals. Its training/test split is unspecified, and there is no harmful-continuation recovery measurement. After Tulu-3 + FalseReject tuning, Gemma-2-2B prefilling ASR on 200 harmful prompts is 48.5%, versus 49.0% for the Tulu-3 baseline (V7 row state partial; significance not stated). SafePath counts Safety Primer emissions: over 8 per sample under PAIR on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, with repetitive emissions shown in its Figure 9. The V7 state can't be determined from this count alone. Neither measure alone establishes robust recovery from harmful continuations.

The records support conditional improvements and include failed robustness tests. Under ordinary prefilling, the data-augmented Llama-2-7B-Chat checkpoint has a harmfulness score of 0.001, versus the original model's 0.831. Under intermediate human rank-based prefilling (RAP) it scores 0.6731 (StrongREJECT scores, not ASR; V7 row state absent). Deep Alignment Gemma-2-9B-IT refusal at prefill depth 100 falls from 90% to 10% after 50 benign Alpaca SFT steps (V7 state for durable protection: absent). Under a safe-sounding-prefix training attack, Deep Token Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct has 0.96% AdvBench safety, versus 3.65% for vanilla SFT (GPT-4o judge).

Durability gives different answers under different threat models. Attack form unlike training: prefill-trained Llama-2-7B-Chat has 34.3% ASR under 100-token random insertion. Evaluation template: after an attack, Soft-SFT realignment of Llama-2-7B-Chat+SQL cuts ASR from 62.1% to 6.3% under the matched self template, but ASR is 36.4% under the raw template (row state partial; task score 0.358 self, 0.001 raw). Removable safeguards and type of later training: SRP ASR is 7.00% with provider mechanisms and 79.50% without under adversarial fine-tuning, and 0.00% versus 20.75% under benign GSM8K fine-tuning (V7 durability absent without them). The phrase also leaves open whether benign-compliance cost counts: Qwen-Audio deep SFT raises benign over-rejection from 1.14% to 85.49%. That row's V7 state is cannot_determine, because it is a utility cost, not a reversal of the safety effect.

Broader coverage is finite and can depend on the trained depth window. Longer prefills and insertions after an initial refusal remain effective; broader protection should not imply arbitrary-depth recovery.

method_sensitivity.what: For trajectory-aligned Qwen2.5-7B on AdvBench injection, OM gives 11.73% ASR and LG gives 5.19%. The Mistral prefilling verdict changes from substantial residual vulnerability under OM to much lower rates under LG.

method_sensitivity.factor: Attack location, span and training window
method_sensitivity.what: Prefill-trained Llama-2-7B random-insertion ASR rises from 18.4% at a 25-token span to 34.3% at 100 tokens. The pack also reports weaker Llama-3.1/Gemma protection beyond the 50-token training span. These comparisons change the attack relative to training.

RESET SFT remains weak against optimization attacks, while SFT+DPO improves robustness. SRP requires reflection placement across both pretraining and post-training; pretraining-only reflections can give no gain or worse results. These are within-study training variants.

On abliterated Qwen2.5-3B, refusal-only training yields refusal score 17.8, explanation-only 81.1 and justification-only 86.2, versus 90.9 for the full extended-refusal model. DeepRefusal without harmful-prefix augmentation has 83.7% prefill ASR versus 0.4% for the full model.
DeepAlign Llama2-7B-Chat harmfulness changes from 0% at 10 shots to 14.2% at 50 and 42.7% at 100. Constrained SFT backdoor ASR is 1.9% without the trigger and 10.9% with it.

The contrastive DeepAlign verdict reports weaker robustness with k=1 and with final- or early-layer training. These settings alter the defense, so its low main-table ASR should not be generalized to arbitrary layer or prefix choices.

Soft-SFT realignment of attacked Llama-2-7B-Chat+SQL (attack=self, defense=self) gives 6.3% ASR under the self evaluation template, versus 62.1% for the attacked, undefended model under self evaluation. Under raw evaluation formatting the realigned model's ASR is 36.4%. Its task scores are 0.358 under self and 0.001 under raw. Gemma-2-9B deep alignment leaves a 19% maximum syntax ASR@10 gap relative to imperative wording.

For DS-Qwen3-8B under adversarial reasoning prefill, answer-only training gives reasoning safety-awareness of 57.8% from 52.4% originally. Full SARA raises it to 75.1%. Final-answer safety (SS) with full SARA is 97.4%, versus 99.4% with answer-only (final-answer-only reward) training and 87.9% for the untreated model. Answer safety and reasoning recovery therefore respond differently to the reward.

Course-Correction reports higher measured correction with longer allowed continuations, including delayed corrections. Corr@10, mean correction and jailbreak ASR answer different questions; high correction does not establish that harmful material was never generated. On Llama2-Chat 7B after DPO, Corr@10 rises from 66.60% to 90.85%, while AutoDAN ASR goes from 54.00% to 52.00%, a small reduction.

The recovery guarantee depends on positive base recovery probability, penalty strength and positional discounting. Its aggregate KL cost grows as the discount approaches 1; this is a formal sensitivity result rather than an observed capability curve.
